# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Wednesday, November 25, 2026

Wednesday edition for 25 November 2026 (IST), covering Tuesday 24 November to Wednesday morning. **The markets reopen today** — pre-open at 09:00, normal session 09:15–15:30, the first session since Monday and the start of a new F&O series; MCX runs a normal commodity session, including gold and silver. **Every index and stock figure below is Monday 23 November's close**: Tuesday was the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday, NSE's 24 November index file answers 404, and the bhavcopy for that date returns the 23 November file byte-identical. IBJA's own block reads "Rates will be uploaded soon" — a normal session not yet posted, a different state from yesterday's "Holiday" — so the domestic benchmark stays on Monday's PM rates until today's AM session posts. **AGLOC's block is read and dated 25 November**: ₹9,728 / ₹9,156 / ₹8,583 on a ₹11,445 jewellery reference, all three unchanged because that reference is Monday's IBJA 916 rate carried forward — one observation, not a fresh move. Wednesday is a two-report day — news and regulation; the weekly analysis desk files on Mondays.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold gives back Monday's 3.90% rebound in one session; silver settles at a new 52-week low
Comex front-month gold **settled at $3,559.90 an ounce on Tuesday 24 November, down $89.30 or 2.45%** — a one-session reversal that took back Monday's 3.90% rebound. It was the **second-lowest settlement of the year**, down four of the past five sessions, **33.06% below the 52-week and record high of $5,318.40** set on 29 January, up only **1.36% from the 52-week low of $3,512.30** set on 20 November, and **down 17.70% year-to-date** (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 24 Nov, 18:52 ET).

Silver fell harder. Comex front-month **settled at $40.760 an ounce, down $2.3870 or 5.53% — a new 52-week low and the lowest settlement since 29 August 2025** — down seven of the past nine sessions, **64.58% below its 52-week high of $115.08** set on 26 January, and **down 41.88% year-to-date and 16.98% month-to-date** (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 24 Nov, 18:53 ET).

On the domestic exchange, MCX's **evening session — the only one open on the holiday — took the December contracts down with it**. **GOLD 04DEC2026 last traded at ₹1,22,250 per 10 g, down ₹3,746 or 2.97%** against a previous close of ₹1,25,996; **SILVER 04DEC2026 last traded at ₹1,45,150 per kg, down ₹9,067 or 5.88%** against ₹1,54,217 (exchange quote board, 24 Nov 23:54–23:55 IST). **These are last-traded prices off the exchange's quote board, not exchange settlements, and no rupee change is derived from them for any other contract.**

The reported reason is hawkish Federal Reserve signalling and firm expectations of a December hike, plus liquidation out of equities forcing investors to free up margin — reported by Reuters via CNBC, and attributed here to the analysts who said it, not to the Fed as an announcement. That piece had spot gold down 2% at $3,556.82 by 15:19 ET after a low of $3,552.46, US gold futures down 2.6% at $3,555.80 and spot silver down 5% at $40.84, with traders — per CME FedWatch — fully pricing a 25 basis point December hike and a 2% chance of 50. **Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, quoted in the same report**: "Gold is struggling to find meaningful support because central banks, led by the Fed, are hawkish," and, on the mechanism, "liquidation from the equity space that is forcing investors to free up margins by closing gold and silver." New York Fed President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation still points toward tighter policy, the pace depending on incoming data — as reported by the same piece, not as a Fed decision.

What comes next is the US October PCE inflation print, due on Wednesday, US time — tonight IST — the last key inflation reading before the Fed's December meeting. At the time of BusinessLine's 24 Nov 14:41 IST report, traders were pricing a **96% chance of a 25 basis point December hike and 4% for 50**; the CNBC piece had them fully pricing 25. These are snapshots that move through the day, quoted with their sources, not forecasts adopted here.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a one-session give-back that retraces Monday's bounce leaves the collateral arithmetic roughly where the weekend left it — the average, not either spot print, governs the ceiling, and two sessions of round-tripping change nothing in it. The mechanism is worked through below, in Gold and LTV.

### Markets reopen at 09:15 after the holiday; GIFT Nifty indicates a gap-up
Today is a normal trading day — the first since Monday. The equity, equity-derivative, currency-derivative, SLB and interest-rate derivative segments run pre-open at 09:00 and a normal session **09:15–15:30**, the start of a new F&O series. NSE's holiday master puts the next equity-segment holiday after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti at **25 December 2026 (Christmas)**, with nothing between. MCX runs a normal commodity session, including gold and silver.

Before the bell, **GIFT Nifty was trading around 25,739, a premium of roughly 234–260 points to the Nifty futures' previous close, pointing to a gap-up open after Monday's sell-off** (NDTV Profit and Mint, 25 Nov morning; Mint at 06:40 IST). An indication is not a close; the gap-up only becomes a fact if today's session prints it.

The overnight backdrop, dated Tuesday 24 November: the **Dow Jones rose 423.39 (0.85%) to 50,018.70**, while the **S&P 500 fell 36.08 (0.50%) to 7,201.09** and the **Nasdaq Composite fell 356.02 (1.48%) to 23,733.54** (NDTV Profit). Asian markets were lower on Wednesday morning — Nikkei −2.48%, Kospi −4.76%. Brent was around $90.77–91.16 a barrel and WTI $81.81, and the dollar index stood at 103.86, off 0.01% (Mint and ET Now, 25 Nov 06:24–06:53 IST) — morning indications, not settlements, and dated as such.

There is no 24 November session to look for anywhere in the sources: the index file for the date answers 404 and the bhavcopy for the date returns the 23 November file byte-identical.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none directly. A holiday means no fresh domestic price discovery for a day, so the 30-day average that governs collateral valuation carries Monday's print rather than a new one when the market reopens.
Sources: [NSE holiday master](https://www.nseindia.com/api/holiday-master?type=trading) · [NDTV Profit, 25 Nov](https://www.ndtvprofit.com/markets/stock-market-today-gift-nifty-to-nasdaq-kospi-selloff-five-key-factors-that-may-drive-sensex-nifty-50-on-november-25-12373070) · [Mint, 25 Nov 06:40 IST](https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/stock-market-outlook-today-25-nov-sensex-nifty-prediction-djia-s-p-nasdaq-gift-nifty-kospi-nikkei-taiwan-cues-11795566965791.html) · [NSE index closes, 23 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/indices/ind_close_all_23112026.csv)

### Monday's close, the last before the bell: banks fell far harder than NBFCs
The last session, Monday 23 November, was a sharp down day led by banks, and the gap between the two indices is the useful read. The **Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35** while the **Nifty NBFC fell only 0.69% to 55,647.61**. The **Nifty 50 fell 1.75% to 25,349.65**, Nifty Financial Services 2.49% to 28,153.50, Nifty PSU Bank 3.25% to 9,559.65 and Nifty Private Bank 3.19% to 30,659.85. Nifty Next 50 fell 1.31% to 72,245.40 and Nifty Metal 3.68% to 11,819.25, while Nifty IT rose 1.69% to 31,850.80. India VIX closed at 17.70, up 0.38 points or 2.18%.

The Sensex — a BSE index, not in the NSE archive — **closed at 82,435.99, down 1,483.72 points or 1.77%** (The Hindu BusinessLine's market wrap).

Among the gold-loan and NBFC names, **Muthoot Finance closed at ₹2,543.30, down 0.28%**, and **IIFL Finance at ₹615.00, up 0.50%**, the two that held their ground. **Manappuram fell 3.39% to ₹271.00**, **Muthoot Microfin 3.23% to ₹160.06**, Muthoot Capital 3.57% to ₹187.33, Bajaj Finance 2.36% to ₹1,095.50 and Cholamandalam 2.33% to ₹1,831.00, while **Shriram Finance rose 2.46% to ₹995.90**. M&M Financial eased 0.50% to ₹286.85, Five Star Business Finance 0.84% to ₹429.35, and CreditAccess Grameen closed up 0.21% at ₹983.80. **Muthoot Finance is a listed peer, not Muthoot Fincorp; Muthoot Microfin is a listed group company, not Muthoot Fincorp either; and every price above belongs to the company whose ticker printed it.**

Institutional flows, NSE provisional and still the latest date in the exchange's file: FII/FPI were **net buyers of ₹5,672.99 crore** (bought ₹23,473.67 crore, sold ₹17,800.68 crore) and DIIs **net sellers of ₹2,760.12 crore** (bought ₹16,505.75 crore, sold ₹19,265.87 crore).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a 3.17% banks fall against a 0.69% NBFC fall is a comparison of two index moves, not evidence about any single lender. Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in either index.

### Muthoot Microfin's independent director Ms Bhama Krishnamurthy has died
Muthoot Microfin **disclosed on 24 November 2026, under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the death of Ms Bhama Krishnamurthy, an independent director of the company (DIN 02196839), with her date of cessation recorded as 24 November 2026**. The company described the loss as irreparable and extended condolences. The disclosure records the cessation, and it says nothing beyond it.

**Muthoot Microfin is a listed subsidiary of Muthoot Fincorp, and this is the subsidiary's board, not the parent's.** The filing is Muthoot Microfin's own, about its own board composition; it is not a Muthoot Fincorp disclosure and not a change to Muthoot Fincorp's own board.

No inference is drawn here: the disclosure says nothing about a replacement appointment, a rating action or board-composition compliance, and none is speculated on. The subsidiary's shares last closed at ₹160.06 on Monday 23 November, down 3.23%, before Tuesday's holiday (NSE bhavcopy).

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none asserted. A listed subsidiary's board composition is the subsidiary's governance item; the parent's filings say nothing about it, and this edition does not reach beyond the disclosure.

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### The EGM was held on 23 November and the proceedings are on the investor page; the outcome is not readable from here
An extraordinary general meeting of Muthoot Fincorp was held on **23 November 2026** on the two items its board had recommended alongside the Q2 filing: the conversion of **40,00,00,000 compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares**, and the reappointment of **Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot for five years from 1 February 2027**. The intimation of the meeting and its proceedings were posted to the investor page **by 24 November**.

**What was resolved is still not readable from here, and this edition does not guess it.** The documents are served through presigned links that expire in 900 seconds, and the bucket refuses unsigned requests; the investor page itself was re-read today and carries **no new documents** — the same 873 distinct document names as yesterday, with the EGM intimation and proceedings still the two newest. Only two facts are re-stated — the meeting was held, and the two documents were posted — and whether the resolutions passed is not inferred.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the proceedings document is the authority on what passed. Until it is readable, the conversion is recorded here only as a board recommendation that an EGM was held on — not a completed capital event — and no effect on reported CRAR is inferred.
Sources: [Muthoot Fincorp investor page — re-read 25 Nov, no new documents](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors) · [BSE: Q2 FY27 filing and board recommendations, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

### Q2 FY27 stands where it was filed: profit doubled, Stage III at 1.07%, CRAR 19.38%
Nothing in today's sources changes the quarter. The standing figures, each on its own date: **PAT of ₹779.41 crore for July–September 2026** against ₹388 crore a year earlier, **H1 PAT of ₹1,485 crore** on total income of ₹6,567 crore, quarterly total income of **₹3,408 crore, up 71% year-on-year**, **Stage III at 1.07%** against 1.41% a year earlier, net Stage III at 0.63%, and **CRAR at 19.38%** — all from the Reg 52 filing of 14 November 2026 (Business Standard, 16 Nov).

On funding, the average cost of borrowing fell 121 basis points to **9.11% in FY26** from 10.32% in FY25, with overseas borrowings at 9.20% of total borrowings at March 2026, commercial paper at 8.92% and bank term loans at 39.69% of the mix, across 67 listed NCD issuances; the average yield on loans was 21.38% against 22.47%, and NIM steady at 12.80% (BusinessLine, updated 12 Nov). The **NCD Tranche I — ₹500 crore (₹200 crore base plus ₹300 crore green shoe), 23 October to 5 November — has been listed on the BSE since 11 November** in the "F" group, rated CRISIL AA/Stable and Brickwork AA+/Stable, with a coupon of 8.56%–9.25%; the final allotted amount has still not been seen in a published source.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the Q2 numbers were struck on a book whose collateral was marked at September prices; gold's move since then is not in them, which is why the coming quarters — not this one — carry the price fall.
Sources: [Business Standard, 16 Nov 13:57 IST](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/quarterly-results/muthoot-fincorp-q2-profit-doubles-to-779-crore-on-better-asset-quality-126111601050_1.html) · [BSE: Q2 FY27 filing, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf) · [BusinessLine on borrowing costs, 12 Nov](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/muthoot-fincorp-diversifies-funding-to-trim-borrowing-cost/article71695055.ece) · [BSE notice 20261109-30, NCD listing](https://www.bseindia.com/downloads/UploadDocs/Notices/20261109-30/20261109-30.pdf)

### IPO status: SEBI's processing list still shows clarifications sought
The draft offer is with SEBI and has not moved. SEBI's draft-offer processing status, **as on 20 November 2026** — the current weekly report — records **Muthoot Fincorp Limited**, coordinating lead manager **Kotak Mahindra Capital Company**, **IPO (Fresh Only)**, a **date of receipt of 13 August 2026** and a **last date of communication of 12 November 2026**, under **Section II — "clarifications are sought by SEBI and response from LM is awaited"**. No observations have been issued; there is no price band and no dates. The report is re-issued weekly at a new URL; the link below is the current one.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the offer is pending at the regulator, not at the company. Nothing in today's sources bears on it.
Sources: [SEBI draft offer processing status, as on 20 Nov 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/nov-2026/1795175784186.pdf)

### Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on related-party transactions with the parent runs to 13 December
A group item on the standing calendar: Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on material related party transactions with Muthoot Fincorp — **up to ₹2,500 crore, including gold-loan assignments and co-lending** — has remote e-voting open from **14 November to 13 December 2026**, with results to be published on or before **15 December**. It is a shareholder approval of a transaction framework, not a new transaction, and it is the listed subsidiary's process; the parent is the related party in it, not the filer.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ballot governs the assignment and co-lending arrangements the two companies use. The result is not known from here and is not predicted; the e-voting window runs to 13 December.

### What the 30-day-average rule does with a two-session round trip
The June 2025 Directions value collateral at the **lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day** (para 17), and require the prescribed LTV to be maintained **on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor** (para 20). Monday's 3.90% bounce and Tuesday's 2.45% give-back therefore cancel at the spot level within two sessions, while the 30-day average keeps rolling — and the average, not either print, is the number that governs the ceiling. **A two-session round trip changes nothing in the arithmetic.**

Worked on IBJA's own 916 series, and labelled an illustration rather than any lender's book: 916 went from **₹1,34,201 per 10 g on 17 November's PM session to ₹1,13,486 on 20 November's PM session, a fall of 15.4% in three sessions**. A loan written at the 75% ceiling against the 17 November reference would sit at about **88.7% of the 20 November reference on the same collateral — above the 85% ceiling that applies to any ticket size**. The division is ₹1,34,201 ÷ ₹1,13,486 = 1.1825, and 75% × 1.1825 = 88.7%.

The background to that arithmetic is already on the record, each item with its own date, and none of it is today's news: the RBI met NBFC, HFC and microfinance chief executives on 23 November (readout, press release 2026-2027/1554); the Economic Times reported on 24 November at 01:11 IST that the RBI asked for greater scrutiny of gold-loan LTVs as prices fall, citing TransUnion CIBIL's gold-loan NPAs at **0.30% at end-August 2026 against 0.16% at 31 March 2026**; Moneycontrol reported on 23 November at 10:04 IST that the RBI has raised the frequency of portfolio reporting over the last 30–45 days, and that loans against gold stood at **₹3.74 trillion in September 2026, up 66.1% year-on-year**; and Crisil Ratings said on 23 November that it expects gold-loan AUM growth to moderate to about **40% in FY27 from 78% in FY26**.

And the round trip itself: 916 at **₹1,14,450 on 23 November's PM session was +0.85% on 20 November**, and Comex gold rose 3.90% on Monday and fell 2.45% on Tuesday, which puts the dollar price roughly back where it started the week. That is a round trip, not a recovery, and it is stated as one.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: this is the mechanism its book runs on, and it is direction-neutral — the average dampens the damage from a fall and equally dampens the relief from a bounce. No Muthoot Fincorp book is described here, and no lender is named as breaching.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

### Nothing new binds an NBFC on 24 or 25 November; the two uncovered releases are bank-scoped
**No RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument dated 24 or 25 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp.** The RBI's press-release and notifications lists, re-fetched twice this morning, both still stand at the 23 November block — byte-identical to yesterday's fetch, nothing added. SEBI's newest circular remains the 17 November review of the commodity derivatives margin framework, with nothing dated 18 to 25 November. IBBI was checked; its footer carried no date string in this fetch, so none is asserted, and no new insolvency instrument dated 24 or 25 November was seen.

Two 23 November press releases not covered in yesterday's edition are both scoped to banks. The **draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions"** (press release 2026-2027/1548) are **a consultation, not a rule in force: comments are due by 14 December 2026**. They propose amendments to the Responsible Business Conduct directions for commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks, and urban and rural co-operative banks — **banks and co-operative banks; no NBFC instrument is in that list, and nothing in it binds Muthoot Fincorp**. reports.content:
# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Wednesday, 25 November 2026 (IST)

Wednesday edition for 25 November 2026 (IST), covering Tuesday 24 November to Wednesday morning; regulator pages read 07:03–07:45 IST. The markets reopen today at 09:15, so market figures elsewhere are Monday 23 November's closes until today's session prints. **No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument dated 24 or 25 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp.** The RBI's press-release and notifications lists, re-fetched twice this morning, both still stand at the 23 November block — byte-identical to yesterday's fetch; SEBI's newest circular remains the 17 November margin-framework review; and IBBI was checked with no update date assertable. What follows is the standing gold-loan rulebook (the mechanism behind this week's collateral arithmetic), the two 23 November press releases not previously covered — both scoped to banks — the administrative SGB redemption price, and the next scheduled decision, the MPC on 2–4 December.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

The one-line position: **nothing new binds the company today.** The 23 November block on the RBI's lists is unchanged since yesterday's edition — four parallel securitisation amendments (Commercial Banks Id=13753, Small Finance Banks Id=13754, NBFCs Id=13755, All India Financial Institutions Id=13756), of which the NBFC one was covered then and takes effect on 1 April 2027 — and no instrument dated 24 or 25 November appears above it. Two 23 November press releases were not covered in that edition and are set out below; both are bank-scoped, and neither touches the company. The RBI has changed no rule on any day covered here.

### The standing rulebook: RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025
The Directions were issued on 6 June 2025 (RBI/2025-26/47 DOR.CRE.REC.26/21.01.023/2025-26), updated on 29 September 2025 by the (1st Amendment) Directions (RBI/2025-26/84 DOR.CRE.REC.52/21.01.023/2025-26), with compliance required by 1 April 2026. Para 15 caps bullet-repayment consumption loans at 12 months, renewable under para 11; para 16 caps ornaments at 1 kg of gold (10 kg silver) and coins at 50 g gold (500 g silver) per borrower; para 17 values collateral at the **lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day**, per IBJA or a SEBI-regulated commodity exchange; para 19 sets maximum LTV at **85%** (loans up to ₹2.5 lakh), **80%** (₹2.5–5 lakh) and **75%** (above ₹5 lakh); para 20 requires the prescribed LTV to be maintained **on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor**; para 40 sets the auction reserve price at not less than 90% of current value, 85% only after two failed auctions; and para 43 requires any auction surplus to be refunded within seven working days of receiving the full proceeds.

Why this rulebook matters this week is the two-session round trip: Monday's 3.90% bounce and Tuesday's 2.45% give-back cancel at the spot level, while para 17's average keeps rolling over the higher prints of October and early November — **the average is the number that governs the ceiling**, and para 20 tests the loan against it continuously, which is why a fall reaches a book with a lag rather than on the day it happens. AGLOC's block dated 25 November 2026 puts the ceiling at ₹9,728 a gram at the 85% band, ₹9,156 at 80% and ₹8,583 at 75%, on a ₹11,445 jewellery reference — all unchanged from 24 November because that reference is Monday's IBJA 916 rate carried forward, not a new quote, so the flatness is the holiday showing through, not a stable market.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these are the Directions its gold-loan book and auction practice run under; nothing in them changed today, and nothing dated 24 or 25 November adds to them.
Sources: [RBI: Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral Directions, 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12859) · [RBI: (1st Amendment) Directions, 29 Sep 2025](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12903) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [AGLOC, block dated 25 Nov 2026](https://www.agloc.org/)

### Draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for EBTs": a consultation due 14 December, and no NBFC is in its scope
The RBI issued for public comment on 23 November 2026 a set of **draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)"** — press release 2026-2027/1548, dated 23 November 2026 and signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager. **It is a draft issued for comments, with feedback due by 14 December 2026; it is not a rule in force, and no rule changed when it appeared.**

Its scope is explicit and it excludes NBFCs. The draft proposes amendments to the Responsible Business Conduct directions for **Commercial Banks (Fifth Amendment), Small Finance Banks (Fifth), Payments Banks (Third), Local Area Banks (Fifth), Regional Rural Banks (Fifth), Urban Co-operative Banks (Fifth) and Rural Co-operative Banks (Fifth)** — banks and co-operative banks. **No NBFC instrument is in that list; the draft does not bind Muthoot Fincorp.** In substance, it proposes to strengthen the June 24, 2026 Amendment Directions on customer protection in fraudulent electronic banking transactions "from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels may be used", and to expand the definition of "negligence by a bank" for uniformity across banks.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none — the scope is banks and co-operative banks. Nothing in the draft touches the company's gold-loan, funding or securitisation rules, and the comment deadline is a banks' consultation to watch rather than a company obligation.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1548, 23 Nov 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64026)

### The 2026 D-SIB list: SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, same buckets as 2025 — banks only
The RBI published the 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks on 23 November 2026 (press release 2026-2027/1547). **SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank remain D-SIBs under the same bucketing as 2025**: SBI in bucket 4 with **0.80% additional CET1**, HDFC Bank in bucket 2 with **0.40%**, and ICICI Bank in bucket 1 with **0.20%**. The list is based on data as on 31 March 2026. **Banks only — no NBFC appears on it, and nothing in it applies to Muthoot Fincorp.**

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none. A D-SIB surcharge is a bank capital requirement; the company's capital position is governed by the NBFC scale-based framework and its own reported CRAR of 19.38% at 30 September 2026.
Sources: [RBI press release 2026-2027/1547, 23 Nov 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64025) · [BSE: Muthoot Fincorp Q2 FY27 filing, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

### The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
The Monetary Policy Committee meets on **2–4 December 2026, with the decision due on 4 December**. The policy repo rate stands at **5.50%**, raised 25 basis points at the 5–7 October meeting, with the stance at calibrated tightening; the SDF is 5.25%, and the MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. October CPI inflation was **6.09% — the first breach of the 6% upper tolerance band in two years** — with food inflation at 8.94% (Business Standard, 13 Nov 15:51 IST). The RBI is inside its pre-policy quiet period between meetings, so no member speaks to the decision before it is announced.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the repo sets the floor under the company's cost of funds, and its last published average cost of borrowing was 9.11% for FY26, with bank term loans at 39.69% of the borrowing mix — the part of the book where a policy move passes through most directly.

cards.title: Gold gives back Monday's 3.90% rebound in one session; silver settles at a new 52-week low
cards.summary: Comex front-month gold settled at $3,559.90 an ounce on Tuesday 24 November, down $89.30 or 2.45% — a one-session reversal that took back Monday's 3.90% rebound. It was the second-lowest settlement of the year , down four of the past five sessions, 33.06% below the 52-week and record high of $5,318.40 set on 29 January, up only 1.36% from the 52-week low of $3,512.30 set on 20 November, and down 17.70% year-to-date (Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar, 24 Nov, 18:52 ET).
cards.impact: a one-session give-back that retraces Monday's bounce leaves the collateral arithmetic roughly where the weekend left it — the average, not either spot print, governs the ceiling, and two sessions of round-tripping change nothing in it. The mechanism is worked through below, in Gold and LTV.

cards.title: Markets reopen at 09:15 after the holiday; GIFT Nifty indicates a gap-up
cards.summary: Today is a normal trading day — the first since Monday. The equity, equity-derivative, currency-derivative, SLB and interest-rate derivative segments run pre-open at 09:00 and a normal session 09:15–15:30 , the start of a new F&O series.
cards.impact: none directly. A holiday means no fresh domestic price discovery for a day, so the 30-day average that governs collateral valuation carries Monday's print rather than a new one when the market reopens.

cards.title: Monday's close, the last before the bell: banks fell far harder than NBFCs
cards.summary: The last session, Monday 23 November, was a sharp down day led by banks, and the gap between the two indices is the useful read. The Nifty Bank fell 3.17% to 62,585.35 while the Nifty NBFC fell only 0.69% to 55,647.61 .
cards.impact: a 3.17% banks fall against a 0.69% NBFC fall is a comparison of two index moves, not evidence about any single lender. Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted and has no share price in either index.

cards.title: Muthoot Microfin's independent director Ms Bhama Krishnamurthy has died
cards.summary: Muthoot Microfin disclosed on 24 November 2026, under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the death of Ms Bhama Krishnamurthy, an independent director of the company (DIN 02196839), with her date of cessation recorded as 24 November 2026 . The company described the loss as irreparable and extended condolences.
cards.impact: none asserted. A listed subsidiary's board composition is the subsidiary's governance item; the parent's filings say nothing about it, and this edition does not reach beyond the disclosure.

cards.title: The EGM was held on 23 November and the proceedings are on the investor page; the outcome is not readable from here
cards.summary: An extraordinary general meeting of Muthoot Fincorp was held on 23 November 2026 on the two items its board had recommended alongside the Q2 filing: the conversion of 40,00,00,000 compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares , and the reappointment of Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot for five years from 1 February 2027 . The intimation of the meeting and its proceedings were posted to the investor page by 24 November .
cards.impact: the proceedings document is the authority on what passed. Until it is readable, the conversion is recorded here only as a board recommendation that an EGM was held on — not a completed capital event — and no effect on reported CRAR is inferred.

cards.title: Q2 FY27 stands where it was filed: profit doubled, Stage III at 1.07%, CRAR 19.38%
cards.summary: Nothing in today's sources changes the quarter. The standing figures, each on its own date: PAT of ₹779.41 crore for July–September 2026 against ₹388 crore a year earlier, H1 PAT of ₹1,485 crore on total income of ₹6,567 crore, quarterly total income of ₹3,408 crore, up 71% year-on-year , Stage III at 1.07% against 1.41% a year earlier, net Stage III at 0.63%, and CRAR at 19.38% — all from the Reg 52 filing of 14 November 2026 (Business Standard, 16 Nov).
cards.impact: the Q2 numbers were struck on a book whose collateral was marked at September prices; gold's move since then is not in them, which is why the coming quarters — not this one — carry the price fall.

cards.title: IPO status: SEBI's processing list still shows clarifications sought
cards.summary: The draft offer is with SEBI and has not moved. SEBI's draft-offer processing status, as on 20 November 2026 — the current weekly report — records Muthoot Fincorp Limited , coordinating lead manager Kotak Mahindra Capital Company , IPO (Fresh Only) , a date of receipt of 13 August 2026 and a last date of communication of 12 November 2026 , under Section II — "clarifications are sought by SEBI and response from LM is awaited" .
cards.impact: the offer is pending at the regulator, not at the company. Nothing in today's sources bears on it.

cards.title: Muthoot Microfin's postal ballot on related-party transactions with the parent runs to 13 December

It is a shareholder approval of a transaction framework, not a new transaction, and it is the listed subsidiary's process; the parent is the related party…
cards.impact: the ballot governs the assignment and co-lending arrangements the two companies use. The result is not known from here and is not predicted; the e-voting window runs to 13 December.

cards.title: What the 30-day-average rule does with a two-session round trip
cards.summary: The June 2025 Directions value collateral at the lower of the average closing price of that purity over the preceding 30 days and the closing price on the preceding day (para 17), and require the prescribed LTV to be maintained on an ongoing basis throughout the tenor (para 20). Monday's 3.90% bounce and Tuesday's 2.45% give-back therefore cancel at the spot level within two sessions, while the 30-day average keeps rolling — and the average, not either print, is the number…
cards.impact: this is the mechanism its book runs on, and it is direction-neutral — the average dampens the damage from a fall and equally dampens the relief from a bounce. No Muthoot Fincorp book is described here, and no lender is named as breaching.

latest_circulars.title: The next scheduled decision: the MPC meets 2–4 December
latest_circulars.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee meets on 2–4 December 2026, with the decision due on 4 December . The policy repo rate stands at 5.50% , raised 25 basis points at the 5–7 October meeting, with the stance changed to calibrated tightening; SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%.
latest_circulars.impact: the repo sets the floor under its cost of funds, and the last published average cost of borrowing was 9.11% for FY26. A 25 basis point hike is not itself the risk; the risk is the pass-through into bank term loans, which were 39.69% of the borrowing mix.

latest_circulars.title: The day's regulatory event: the RBI's NBFC/HFC meeting, and the gold-loan scrutiny reported out of it
latest_circulars.summary: The RBI met the managing directors and chief executives of select NBFCs, including government NBFCs, HFCs and microfinance institutions, in Mumbai on 23 November, per its own press release 2026-2027/1554 signed by Brij Raj, Chief General Manager. Representatives of Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC participated; all four Deputy Governors attended with other senior officers; the MD and CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
latest_circulars.impact: the scrutiny is sector-wide; its own Stage III is 1.07% at 30 September 2026, a lagging indicator against a fall that mostly happened after that date. No supervisory action against any named lender is reported.

latest_circulars.title: The 2026 D-SIB list: SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, same buckets as 2025 — banks only
latest_circulars.summary: The RBI published the 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks on 23 November 2026 (press release 2026-2027/1547). SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank remain D-SIBs under the same bucketing as 2025 : SBI in bucket 4 with 0.80% additional CET1 , HDFC Bank in bucket 2 with 0.40% , and ICICI Bank in bucket 1 with 0.20% .
latest_circulars.impact: none. A D-SIB surcharge is a bank capital requirement; the company's capital position is governed by the NBFC scale-based framework and its own reported CRAR of 19.38% at 30 September 2026.

latest_circulars.title: Draft Amendment Directions on "Preventive Safeguards for EBTs": a consultation due 14 December, and no NBFC is in its scope

It is a draft issued for comments, with feedback due by 14 December 2026; it is not a rule in force, and no rule changed when it appeared.
latest_circulars.impact: none — the scope is banks and co-operative banks. Nothing in the draft touches the company's gold-loan, funding or securitisation rules, and the comment deadline is a banks' consultation to watch rather than a company obligation.

latest_circulars.summary: RBI cancelled the registrations of 13 NBFCs and one housing finance company that surrendered them: six left the business, five qualified as unregistered Type I NBFCs, and three ceased to exist after a merger, dissolution or strike-off. The Type I route is open to NBFCs with assets under ₹1,000 crore that take no public funds and have no customer interface.
latest_circulars.impact: none. Muthoot Fincorp takes public funds and deals with customers, so it stays a registered NBFC; the exemption is relevant only to small group investment companies.

latest_circulars.title: RBI cancels Certificate of Registration of 49 NBFCs
latest_circulars.summary: RBI cancelled the certificates of registration of 49 NBFCs under Section 45-IA(6) of the RBI Act, through orders dated 1 to 29 October 2026; 43 of them have registered offices in West Bengal, 41 in Kolkata. RBI did not give the grounds for each cancellation, and the companies can no longer carry on non-banking financial business.
latest_circulars.impact: none directly. Any business partner, co-lending counterparty or loan-sourcing entity that relies on an NBFC registration should be checked against RBI's list.

latest_circulars.title: RBI deputy governor: microfinance FOIR cap stays at 50%, income limit under review
latest_circulars.summary: This is a speech, not a circular, so no rule changes. Deputy Governor Murmu said on 13 Nov that excluding the principal of some loans from the 50% FOIR calculation "would defeat this purpose", that the ₹3 lakh household-income ceiling will be reviewed, and that credit bureaus have been told to move microfinance records out of the consumer segment.
latest_circulars.impact: the FOIR rule and the ₹3 lakh ceiling are unchanged for Muthoot Microfin and any group microfinance lending; a revised income threshold would come only through an amendment to the microfinance Directions.
